steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté ham, onions, and pineapple chunks in hot butter for about 5 minutes.

Combine pineapple juice, vinegar, brown sugar, mustard, and cornstarch in a separate medium bowl; mix well and pour over ham mixture in the skillet. Stir well and allow to heat through and thicken, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Pineapple Dinner
raw_recipe.description: This ham dinner with sautéed onions, chunks of ham, and pineapple in a sweet and tangy sauce is a tasty, family-friendly way to use leftover ham.
raw_recipe.name: Ham and Pineapple Dinner

review.reviewBody: I added some shredded carrots and diced up a jalepeno to add. That made it PERFECT because otherwise it would have been too sweet. It gave it a bite (but one my 2 year old could handle) and the sauce toned down the jalepeno. The sauce is pretty thick but still good. We had it over white rice. I only had 3/4 cup of pineapple juice, so I added apple juice to make it the right amount.

This was very tasty. I used leftover brown sugar maple glazed Thanksgiving Ham. I had some glaze left so mixed some apple cider vinegar in it and it was perfect. Threw everything into crockpot and set it on Low for the day Added some green pepper chunks in last 30 minutes. The ham melted in your mouth. Served it over rice and husband said it was a keeper.

I made this for house dinner. Three of my housemates liked it a lot, though I personally found it very sweet. I think I could have left all of the sugar out and just let the pineapple be the sweetness. 

I cooked in a cup of broccoli, 1 cup of shredded carrots, 1 cup of shredded red cabbage, a handful of mushrooms, and 1 whole red onion.

 I served this over half quinoa, half white rice cooked in a rice cooker with a heaping spoonful of coconut oil = coconut rice.

I liked the idea of this for leftover ham. I wish the recipe had mentioned that there would not be enough pineapple juice in the canned pineapple. I used orange juice which took away from the pineapple flavour. I added 3 tablespoons of soy sauce to balance out the sweet and sour and a clove of garlic. If I make it again I will use a regular onion and use the green onion as a garnish. I also put the pineapple in the pan first to reduce the juice and even brown it a little, then I added the other vegetables using olive oil instead of butter.

I wanted a lighter version of this recipe so I left out the brown sugar and cornstarch. I reduced the apple cider vinegar to 1 tbsp, used a sweet onion instead of scallions, added another tbsp of butter. I added a bit of green pepper and sauteed them with the onion, then added the cut-up ham, pineapple chunks, and juice and heated everything through. I served it atop steamed rice and the "sauce" mixed nicely with it. I'll make this again!!

The only changes I made was to add chunks of sweet onion and I sautéed the sweet onion and ham together first. Then I dumped all the ingredients into a crockpot (minus the cornstarch) on low until I was ready to serve. I added in the cornstarch to thicken the sauce at the end and served at a dinner party with jasmine rice. It was a smash hit!

This was really good. I fried up about a quarter cup of sweet Maui onions along with the white parts of the green onion, and saved the green parts for garnish. Also threw in some sliced carrots. I used a fresh pineapple and squeezed almost a cup of juice out, so I added a bit more from a can. Instead of apple cider vinegar, I used a quarter cup of red wine. It was great! Not strong at all and balanced out the sweetness of the pineapple and brown sugar. Served over quinoa. We will do this again for sure!

It was pretty good, if maybe a little bit too sweet. I also think the sauce thickened up just a bit too much - congealed rather than 'saucy'. I'd cut back on both the brown sugar and cornstarch slightly. I did add veggies (broccoli, carrots, and mushrooms) as many other reviewers did, and sauteed those before adding the onion, garlic (an addition) and ham into the pan. Served over white rice. Good use for leftover ham.

This recipe is terrific. I served mine over Orzo (cuz I don’t care for white rice). But you could totally use any style of rice, Saffron, egg noodles, or whatever. I didn’t have green onions, so I just chopped up purple onion cuz it’s what I had - about a quarter cup in a frying pan. I sauteed them in the pan with the butter, then I added the drained pineapples and ham and turned it off (I used the left-over country ham from breakfast). The recipe called for 1-1/3 cups of pineapple juice, but I only had about 1 cup of the juice from the pineapple can, so I topped it off with orange juice in my fridge. I warmed the juice & apple cider vinegar on the stove with the brown sugar & Dijon mustard (since I don’t know what “prepared mustard” is). Then I poured it into a bowl and whisked in the cornstarch by hand and poured it all over the pineapples, ham & onion in the pan - Put on medium heat until thick. Note: Be careful while stirring the pineapples & ham, so it doesn’t turn to mush.

This is so easy and quite good! Think sweet and sour ham. I did add veggies. I first sauteed bell peppers, onions, and broccoli in butter (and added a little ginger-garlic paste). I only used 3 TBSP of the cider vinegar, and did serve over rice. What a great way to use leftover ham, and it made a quick and easy and yummy dinner. 
I'm considering making this as a freezer meal in the future. (Throw everything in a bag and freeze. Cook in crockpot later.) I'm sure it will be slightly different, but definitely worth the try!
We substituted pineapple chunks with mango and pineapple juice with OJ. Added 1 jalapeno, shredded carrots, broccoli, garlic and a bit of ginger. Really tasty.

This was a fast easy meal. By the time the rice was ready, the rest was finished. I was expecting more of a sweet and sour flavor, but this was more pineapple and mustard. It was fine, but a bit bland overall, and maybe some more vinegar plus some red pepper would bring more life to the party? This is fine, but I wanted something more. This is like getting a vanilla fudge sundae when you were expecting a banana split.
This was easy and tasty. Everyone liked it. Will make again.
I was looking for recipes form left over ham. Made this and we loved it! Easy to make with great flavors. The next time I would use chopped onion in place of the green onion for more onion flavor.
My Mother in law made this recipe for my husband from a Good Housekeeping recipe many years ago. Not my taste. I found this close to hers made it for my H and he loved it. No changes. Thank you
I added chopped green bell peppers.

Worked out good! Wanted to make it with orzo, but I ended up with just minute rice. Grabbed two cans of pineapple chunks thinking it would be enough juice, but it ended up just being about a cup worth. So I mixed with orange juice to get to the 2 1/3 cup juice I needed. Was a great way to use up ham from the other night. Literally spent 10$ at the store to grab the last few things, had everything else. Great meal, will save this for another time!
Add onions and peppers. Use chicken broth instead of pineapple juice.
Made it for dinner. Added broccoli to the restaurant ipe. Family loved the flavors. Sauce isn't too sweet or thick like other dishes.

We always use the leftover hame when we bake a ham to make this recipe. Sometimes swap in any other juice if we don't have pineapple and if using canned pineapple we include the juice from the can. I chop up some green onion and mix it in right before serving. Have fresh carrot an celery sticks with cucumber slices and serve it on basmati rice. Absolutely a crowd pleaser.
